text.p: Sherwin-Williams Co. said Thursday its profits rose by 16 percent in the fourth quarter and by 14 percent for the year, helped by a number of acquisitions and increased paint store sales.
The company said its net income for the fourth quarter rose to $39.1 million, or 45 cents a share, from $33.8 million, or 39 cents a share.
Sales rose by 29 percent to $958.8 million from $740.9 million.
The Cleveland-based company also announced that its board had authorised a two-for-one split of its stock.
For the full year Sherwin-Williams said its net income rose to $229.1 million, or $2.65 a share, from $200.7 million, or $2.34 a share.
Sales for the year, helped by acquisitions, jumped 26 percent to $4.13 billion from $3.27 billion.
The company said net sales in its paint store division rose by 13 percent to $2.41 billion last year, with sales at stores opened at least a year improving by 10 percent.

It added that the paint store division's annual operating profit increased 30 percent to $206.3 million, as a result of volume gains and the continuing containment of selling and administrative costs.
Sherwin-Williams said its coatings unit's annual net sales increased 51.4 percent to $1.71 billion, helped by a number of acquisitions.

The company said acquisitions made in 1995 and 1996, the largest of which was Pratt & Lambert United Inc. last January, gave it growth opportunities in the dealer, mass merchandiser, automotive and speciality markets.
"We are pleased with the contributions that are beginning to be made by our acquisitions as the integration process continues," Chairman John Breen said in a statement.
"The operating profit contributions during 1996 from Pratt & Lambert United Inc. and our other acquisitions exceeded the related cost of financing the acquisitions."

In a separate development, the Environmental Protection Agency said Thursday that Sherwin-Williams had agreed to pay $4.7 million in civil penalties and $1.1 million in costs to clean up pollution around a plant in Chicago.
Sherwin-Williams' stock gained 25 cents to $55.625 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
